transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Michael Torres (Helix ML Eng); Sara Patel (Helix Product); Evan Cho (Helix Infra); Nina Gomez (Helix Data QA)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Reviewed latest quantization runs (INT8/FP8) on LLM-3B variant; small quality deltas noted in list/greeting prompts.
- FP8 gave ~22% throughput improvement vs FP16 with 3-5% quality delta; INT8 gave ~38% throughput but had edge-case regressions on legal/long-list prompts.
- Discussed KV cache behavior: INT8 path currently disables some KV optimizations leading to p95 latency spikes on warm cache misses.
- Agreed next steps: focused 1k-sample eval, share traffic profile, schedule infra deep-dive, tentative limited canary with fallback to baseline.

Topics / Agenda:
- Quick recap (Alex) [00:00]
- Run results walkthrough (Priya) [00:42]
- Customer observations from staging (Michael/Nina) [06:05]
- KV cache and latency root cause (Priya/Evan) [18:30]
- Rollout/fallback and SLA impact (Alex/Sara) [31:10]
- Actions and next steps (Jordan) [45:20]

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for squeezing this in, we got about 50 minutes so we'll try to keep it tight. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Speaker 1 (maybe Jordan): Jordan here, CSM.
[00:18] Priya (SE): Priya, Redwood SE.
[00:22] Michael (Helix): Michael, ML eng.
[00:25] Sara (Helix): Sara, product.
[00:28] Evan (Helix): Evan, infra.
[00:30] Nina (Helix): Nina, data QA.
[00:36] Alex: Cool. Priya you want to walk through the latest experiment results?
[00:42] Priya: Yep, I posted the spreadsheet earlier this morning — link in the deck note, drive.google.com/quant-pilot-metrics (note: shortened in transcription). So we ran three forks off the LLM-3B base: standard FP16 baseline, our FP8 build, and an INT8 build. Each run used the same seed prompt set w/ 10 warm-ups, 1000 requests per config in the smoke run, and then a 100-sample manual sweep for edge-cases.
[01:30] Priya: Summary numbers: FP8 shows about 18-25% throughput improvement depending on sequence length distribution; INT8 is more aggressive at 35-42% throughput gain but with a slightly higher variance. Latency p50/p95 improved accordingly, but we saw p99 spikes in INT8 for certain prompt shapes.
[02:10] Michael: Can you clarify "prompt shapes" — is that long lists vs single-turn QA?
[02:15] Priya: Yeah exactly, long enumerations, bulleted lists, and legal multi-sentence prompts. Those seem to produce slightly different softmax distributions and the quantized kernels end up with tiny numerical shifts that cascade on generation probability for later tokens.
[02:50] Nina: We ran some of our synthetic customer flows — greetings, multi-step forms, and legal disclaimers — and noticed a few higher scoring hallucinations on INT8 in the legal text area. Not many but enough to fail our threshold on a couple of guardrails.
[03:20] Alex: When you say "higher scoring hallucinations" is that human-eval delta or rouge/embedding-based metric?
[03:28] Nina: Mostly human-review flagged and then a small delta on our semantic similarity threshold; it's not huge but it matters for compliance flows.
[04:05] Priya: To add: FP8 kept quality within 1-2% of baseline on the sampled metrics; INT8 drifted more, about 3-7% on targeted legal prompts.
[04:40] Michael: Are these drifts deterministic? Like always the same failure pattern?
[04:45] Priya: Some are repeatable, others are stochastic. We saw a cluster where INT8 produced a different token at position ~24 in a few legal templates consistently.
[05:10] Evan: On the infra side, we noticed that when the cache is cold, INT8 paths are slower at p95; warm cache is fine. I dug into the profiling and it looks like the INT8 kernel currently bypasses a fused KV path in our runtime — probably because of quantized memory layout mismatch. So there's a software path fallback causing a spike.
[05:50] Priya: Yeah we call that the KV cash (transcription: cash) mismatch sometimes in notes — it's basically the cache pointer alignment. On INT8 we sometimes lose the fast path.
[06:20] Alex: That explains p99 spikes. Is that pure software fixable or do we need a recompile/quantization tweak?
[06:30] Priya: Likely both. Short term: we can add a hotfix to re-enable the fused KV for the common sequence lengths; medium term: a quantization layout refactor. Hotfix should cut the p95 spikes by ~60% based on micro-benchmarks.
[07:05] Michael: How risky is the hotfix? Does it change output determinism?
[07:12] Priya: Minimal risk, it's an execution-path change to prefer the fused kernel where alignment conditions are met. It won't change the quantization params themselves. We still need to validate with a 1k evaluation run.
[07:40] Sara: From product standpoint we care about user-visible regressions only. If INT8 gives us 35% cost improvement but fails on 0.5% of legal flows, we need a hard stop.
[07:58] Alex: Totally. The pragmatic path we proposed is canarying: route a small percentage of traffic to INT8 with immediate fallback to baseline on guardrail triggers. That lets you capture real traffic behavior without full exposure.
[08:20] Priya: We can set up a routed policy in Redwood console: e.g., 1% steady-state, ramp to 5% if metrics hold for 24h, with automatic fallback to FP16 on any quality regression. We'll attach the routing config as a stub.
[08:44] Evan: What are the observability hooks needed? We need token-level diff traces and human-flag alerts tied to the guardrail rules.
[08:55] Jordan: We already instrument token-level cost/latency in the pilot sheet, but we'll add a QC column for guardrail flags and a webhook to your incident channel.
[09:20] Priya: Also worth noting: FP8 retains KV fused path so it doesn't show those cold-cache spikes; it's a sweet spot for many workloads.
[09:40] Michael: What's the delta in wall-clock latency p95 between FP16 baseline and FP8 for our median sequence length?
[09:47] Priya: For Helix's median sequence length (approx 128 tokens), FP8 p95 is about 12% lower than FP16; INT8 p95 is about 28% lower but with the occasional spike to higher than baseline on cold-cache.
[10:20] Nina: We did some A/B user tests on small sets; FP8 had no significant regression; INT8 had 2 fails out of 200 in the legal prompt set.
[10:40] Alex: Okay, let's talk numbers people care about — cost savings, throughput, and the SLA impact. Priya, can you share the projected cost per 1M tokens?
[10:50] Priya: Roughly: FP16 baseline is $X (redacted in transcript), FP8 is ~20-30% cheaper, INT8 ~40% cheaper. Will put exact numbers in the sheet.
[11:10] Michael: For procurement we need a risk-adjusted estimate; is the fallback policy automated so we don't need manual ops to flip?
[11:20] Alex: Yes, Redwood routing policies can auto-fallback on guardrails; we can wire that to an on-call channel but it doesn't require manual toggling.
[11:40] Priya: On the regression side, some failure modes correlate strongly with long tail prompt tokens that hit specific attention patterns. We can add a heuristics-based prefilter to route those to FP16 or FP8 rather than INT8.
[12:05] Sara: Could we surface to the product team which prompt templates are risky so we can rewrite them?
[12:12] Nina: We'll surface examples, but some are regulatory text we can't rewrite.
[12:25] Alex: Understood. On rollout cadence — recommended approach: 1) FP8 wider rollout if Helix ready; 2) INT8 canary with strict guardrails and KV hotfix before ramp.
[12:42] Priya: Priya here — quick note on evaluation methodology: the 1k-sample eval should include stratified buckets: greetings, short QA, long lists, legal disclaimers, and multi-turn flows. We'll also compute semantic similarity, ROUGE-ish metrics, and human pass/fail.
[13:10] Michael: We'll provide the 200 production-like prompts from staging to seed that stratified eval by 2026-06-14.
[13:25] Alex: Great. Evan, can you speak to network and instance profiles — anything we should be aware of?
[13:32] Evan: We're using A100-ish in staging and scaling to smaller Ampere instances in prod; network p99 can hit 120ms during bursts, but avg is under 30ms. Those network spikes could exacerbate cold-cache p99s.
[13:55] Priya: Good to know — that means some p99 spikes credited to INT8 might be partially network; we'll add request-level traces to separate compute vs network.
[14:20] Michael: Regarding the hotfix timeline, what's realistic?
[14:25] Priya: We can push a hotfix branch in ~3 business days for testing, then 2-3 days of staging validation. So roughly 6 business days end-to-end to validate.
[14:40] Sara: Does the hotfix require model recompilation or just runtime swap?
[14:44] Priya: Mostly runtime change. Model artifacts remain the same. There may be a small repackage to enable the fused path at runtime.
[15:05] Alex: Let's talk about rollback strategies if we hit a regression in canary.
[15:10] Priya: Auto fallback is first line. Second line: instant route-change to FP8 or FP16. Third: we can pin a model version in the console until we fix root cause.
[15:25] Jordan: I'll add those to the canary runbook.
[15:30] Michael: For our audit/compliance, we need full audit logs and cryptographic proofs that fallback happened if it did — any blocking gaps?
[15:40] Alex: Redwood console provides audit logs and event traces; for cryptographic proof we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for signing critical events — that's part of Redwood Private feature set; but for hosted pilots we can provide verifiable logs with timestamps.
[16:05] Sara: Great. Any legal sign-off needed for canary?
[16:09] Michael: Our legal will want to review failure modes but it's mostly product approval; we'll loop them in after we have the 1k-eval.
[16:22] Priya: One more data note: we also ran a synthetic temperature sweep, INT8 shows slightly more variance when sampling temperature >0.8, so for creative generative flows INT8 may be less stable. For deterministic templates it was fine.
[16:50] Nina: That matches our findings — high-temperature configs spawned more divergence.
[17:05] Alex: Ok back to canary and rollout schedule proposal: Jordan?
[17:10] Jordan: Proposed timeline in the pilot doc:
- 2026-06-12: Redwood uploads canary runbook + routing policy template
- 2026-06-14: Helix provides production prompt set and traffic profile
- 2026-06-17: Redwood shares 1k-sample eval results (Priya)
- 2026-06-18: Latency/infra deep-dive (30 min)
- 2026-06-20: Start canary (1% traffic) if metrics clear

[17:55] Michael: That seems reasonable. A question on observability: can we get token-level diffs for a sampled percent of fallingbacks?
[18:05] Priya: Yes, we can capture token diffs and attach them to the incident row; also we can redact PII automatically.
[18:20] Evan: Anything special we need to do with our CI to enable the routed policy?
[18:25] Alex: Redwood exposes a small API and Terraform module for routing; we'll share a sample. It just needs an API key and the route rules.
[18:40] Michael: Who's owning the test harness? Helix or Redwood?
[18:45] Jordan: Hybrid. Redwood will run the 1k eval and produce the artifacts; Helix will run the same harness in their staging for cross-validation.
[19:05] Sara: A question about model variants — can we pin different quantization profiles to different customer segments? e.g., enterprise tenants get FP8 while public tenants get INT8?
[19:18] Priya: Yes, routing can be per-tenant or per-route; you can pin profiles to customer groups or flags.
[19:30] Michael: Great. Anything else on risk?
[19:35] Nina: Just that our QA threshold for legal text is very strict; we may block INT8 unless we see zero fails in the 1k eval.
[19:45] Alex: Understood — that's why canary with fallback is safer so you only touch a slice.
[20:00] Priya: Quick note: the FP8 path is the lower-risk win; recommend trying FP8 first wide unless Helix needs max cost savings immediately.
[20:12] Michael: Product prefers FP8 initially. We'll aim for FP8 ramp and run INT8 in parallel experiments.
[20:20] Evan: On instrumentation I'll add trace headers and pprof dumps for any canary failures. That should help root-cause.
[20:30] Alex: Cool. Any blockers on legal/compliance to proceed?
[20:35] Sara: We'll get legal looped after the 1k eval. No immediate block.
[21:00] Priya: I'll outline the exact stratification for the 1k eval in the sheet. Also will include how we measure hallucination risk via human review + semantic sims.
[21:20] Michael: For the pilot metrics, can you include a column for delta-to-baseline and another for % of guardrail triggers?
[21:30] Priya: Yep.
[21:40] Jordan: I'll share the updated pilot tracker and invite Helix to edit.
[21:48] Alex: Are there any questions about timelines?
[21:52] Michael: No, just one more — is there any precedence (other customers) for immediate rollback automation in the field?
[22:00] Priya: We have a prior case (anonymized) where a canary triggered fallback within 90s because our guardrail hit; automated rollback worked as designed. We'll redact specifics but can share a short case note.
[22:20] Alex: Great. We're nearing the end of the hour so let's confirm action items.
[22:30] Jordan: Action items as discussed — I'll recap.
[22:40] Priya: Also will attach the micro-benchmarks showing the fused KV hotfix impact.
[22:50] Michael: We'll send the 200 prompts and clarify which are regulatory — helps prioritize.
[23:10] Nina: We'll do a quick human review pass on the 1k once it's up to flag obvious fails.
[23:25] Alex: OK wrapping up — thanks everyone.

Recap / Closing notes:
- Short term: Redwood to deliver 1k-sample eval and hotfix branch for KV fused path; Helix to provide production prompt set and traffic profile.
- Canary approach: start 1% traffic for INT8 only after hotfix, auto-fallback enabled; FP8 recommended for wider rollout sooner.
- Observability: token-level diffs, webhook to incident channel, audit logs available.
- Timeline: primary dates in pilot doc; Jordan to share updated tracker (drive + redwood link).
